<!-- generated by agent-scripts/gen_skills.py — do not edit; edit templates/review_diff.md.tmpl for shared wording or gen_skills.py's CAPABILITY_TABLE / *_PARAMS tables for harness-specific wording, then regenerate -->

Review the staged diff for bugs before it is committed. The input is a
worktree path — from `$ARGUMENTS`, or from the skill that delegated here; none
given means the current directory. The reviewer only reads; you triage and fix.

## 1. Stage
Stage every intended change in the worktree, and nothing unrelated. Then
check three things. `git -C <worktree> diff --cached --stat` must not be
empty. Empty means there is nothing to review: the reviewer line is
"no review ran: nothing staged"; go to step 5 (a caller like `backlog-item`
still continues to `land`). `git -C <worktree> diff --stat` must be empty — the
reviewer reads files from disk, so an unstaged edit would make it review code
that is not what gets committed. `git -C <worktree> status --porcelain` shows
no untracked file (`??`) that belongs to this change — stage it, or confirm it
is unrelated.

## 2. Review
Run one cross-model review round. Use one `--run-id` for the whole loop
(e.g. `review-diff-<branch>-<unix-time>`):

```bash
python3 ~/.agent-toolkit/scripts/second_opinion.py review --diff --dir <worktree> --run-id <run-id> --exclude-backend pi
```

The reviewer is the label it prints (`Second opinion via <label>:`).

Refused as too large ("ruled out by payload size")? Split the diff, never
drop hand-written code: first leave out generated copies whose source
(template, params) is in the review — `--diff-path . --diff-path ':!<glob>'` —
but keep one rendered copy per changed template, so the rendering itself is
read. Still too large? Review path groups with one call each (`--diff-path
<paths>`, run-id `<run-id>-<group>`). Every staged file lands in some group.

It exits nonzero (no backend installed, or every backend failed)? Fall back:
print the same prompt — the same command with `--prompt-only` in place of
`--run-id`, keeping any `--diff-path` — and hand it verbatim to a fresh
same-model subagent via the `delegate` tool (harness `pi`). Tell it the worktree path to read
from, and to read only, never edit files. The reviewer is
then "same-model subagent (fallback: <why>)". That fails too? The reviewer
is "no review ran: <why>" — go to step 5. Never skip the review silently, and
never review the diff yourself in this context: a self-review of your own
diff is the blind spot this skill exists to remove.

## 3. Triage
Read the cited lines, then decide each finding: **fix**, or **reject** with a
one-line reason grounded in the code ("already handled at file:line", "this
input cannot reach here"). A real issue outside this change is a reject that
also gets a backlog offer (the shared instructions file's proactive-capture rule).
"No findings." → go to step 5.

## 4. Fix and re-review
Fix every **fix** finding — for a bug, a failing regression test first. Re-run
the repo's full suite and its lint/format checks, re-stage, and go back to
step 2. Max 2 review rounds in total. After round 2, stop looping: a finding
still unresolved goes into the table as **open**.

## 5. Report
Print this block. It is the output contract: the caller's commit gate
(`land`) shows it as-is. Do not commit here.

```
Reviewer: <label | same-model subagent (fallback: why) | no review ran: why>
Rounds: <n>

| # | Finding (file:line) | Severity | Decision | Reason or fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
```
